stimulus.title: Cooling curve of Compound X
stimulus.text: A 25.0 g sample of liquid Compound X (molar mass 78.11 g/mol) at 30.0 °C is placed in a cooling bath that removes energy from it at a steady 50.0 J/s. A probe records its temperature.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the freezing point of Compound X.

rubric.point: 5.5 °C, the temperature of the flat part

parts.sample: 5.5 °C: the temperature stays at 5.5 °C while the liquid freezes (the flat part of the curve).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the molar enthalpy of fusion of Compound X, in kJ/mol.

rubric.point: Energy removed during freezing = plateau time × 50.0 J/s = 63.2 s × 50.0 J/s = 3160 J
Divides by moles (25.0 g ÷ 78.11 g/mol = 0.3201 mol): ΔHfus = +9.87 kJ/mol (positive, since melting absorbs energy)

parts.sample: The plateau lasts 84.5 s − 21.3 s = 63.2 s, so the energy removed is 63.2 s × 50.0 J/s = 3160 J = 3.16 kJ. Moles: 25.0 g ÷ 78.11 g/mol = 0.3201 mol. Freezing released 3.16 kJ ÷ 0.3201 mol = 9.87 kJ/mol, so ΔHfus = +9.87 kJ/mol (melting absorbs the same energy that freezing releases).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain, at the particle level, why the temperature stays constant from 21.3 s to 84.5 s even though energy is still being removed.

rubric.point: The energy removed comes from forming attractions (intermolecular forces) between molecules as they lock into the solid, not from slowing the molecules, so their average kinetic energy (temperature) stays the same
accept: potential energy decreases while kinetic energy stays constant
energy is released as intermolecular attractions form

parts.sample: During freezing, molecules settle into fixed positions and form attractions with their neighbors. Forming these attractions releases energy, which is what the bath removes. The molecules do not slow down on average, so their average kinetic energy, and the temperature, stays constant until all the liquid has frozen.
